name: Mexico City
literature_vertical_cm_per_yr: -30 to -40 in eastern/northern lakebed bowls (up to -50 historically)
literature_sources: Chaussard et al. (2014), Remote Sensing of Environment
agreement_note: After PC10 re-referenced to SW volcanic margin (-99.184E, 19.377N), 120-day peak rose from -4.4 to -7.0 cm LOS (-9.7 cm vertical est., ~-29.5 cm/yr vertical est.), matching the lower-to-mid range of published -30 to -40 cm/yr rates and NASA's >2 cm/month release. Valid fraction 63.9%; remaining spread [-8.0, -4.6] reflects alt_ref 1 inside Ecatepec.
press_summary_gate_note: Approved after off-basin volcanic margin re-run (-7.0 cm LOS / -9.7 cm vertical est. over 120 d); do not claim Mexico City as a first-ever NISAR measurement due to NASA-JPL Oct 2025-Jan 2026 release.

first_nisar_measurement.evidence: NASA-JPL already released preliminary NISAR L-band InSAR subsidence results for Mexico City (Oct 2025-Jan 2026 acquisitions, >2 cm/month). Cannot claim first NISAR measurement.
first_nisar_measurement.atlas_first_claim_note: Multi-basin standardized atlas phrasing must use qualified (to our knowledge) only after excluding Mexico City from any individual-first claim.
